requirements.requirement: Make the existing /srv/inventory tree owned by inventorysvc and readable by inventory-readers while denying access to other ordinary users.
requirements.summary: The executor created the missing service identity and reader group, set the entire observed tree to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, used directory mode 2750 and file mode 0640, and directly demonstrated owner read/write, reader-group read-only access, and denial for an unrelated user. These properties persisted after restart.
The same two files remained present with unchanged sizes and SHA-256 hashes from the prepared baseline through the repair and post-restart verification.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using changes compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were identical before and after execution and restart. The implementation used existing platform utilities and account/permission mechanisms; the trace contains no package installation or upgrade.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the reboot was acknowledged and observed through disconnection, the post-restart boot ID differed, and the system, identities, permissions, access behavior, and data recovered correctly. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot transition.
limitations: Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating inventorysvc and inventory-readers was a necessary prerequisite (cmd-67b76650d11b4df4); changing ownership and modes directly implemented the repair (cmd-384a4b29d9a94854); and scheduling the reboot served the required provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-1a38ccffd6ca4f7f). The other commands were read-only verification or restart polling. After execution there were no failed services, package health remained good, socket exposure was unchanged apart from post-reboot process identifiers, and temporary-file differences were normal boot-specific systemd directories. No abandoned transient restart unit or other unwanted residue is shown.
